🇲🇽🚗 <u>RECORD CAR SALES, TARIFFS AND ALL</u>

Mexicans bought 885,349 new light vehicles from January to July, up 5.0% and the best seven-month run since INEGI began keeping the record in 2005; July alone added 130,831 units (+3.4%). The domestic market keeps expanding even as Washington threatens the very auto sector its economy leans on.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>THE PAN'S SHOWCASE RUNS ON POVERTY WAGES</u>

In Querétaro, the PAN's model state, 41% of workers earn just one to two minimum wages — now the largest and fastest-growing income bracket, jumping from 293,437 to 501,440 people in a single year (+70.9%), according to INEGI's ENOE. The "competitive" state where the paychecks are smallest.

🇲🇽🚆 <u>CDMX BUILDS: 3,600 WORKS, 13,000 HOMES</u>

Mexico City will close Clara Brugada's second year with more than 3,600 public works: 13,000 new homes, 100 of 140 planned kilometers of electric transit already running, and 200,000 new streetlights along 600 km of women's safety routes. In the neighborhoods where drainage was rebuilt, flooding dropped 90% despite heavier rains.

🇲🇽💰 <u>ONE TRILLION PESOS, STRAIGHT TO THE PEOPLE</u>

In two years Sheinbaum's government has channeled more than 1 trillion pesos in direct social investment to 42 million Mexicans — 14.1 million seniors, 1.8 million people with disabilities, 2.16 million farmers getting fertilizer support. "El dinero público es dinero del pueblo y no de los gobernantes," she said. Over the same stretch homicides fell 46% and unemployment sits at 2.9%.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>MEXICO WRITES ITS OWN STEEL INTO THE RULES</u>

For the first time ever, Mexican-made steel now counts toward the national-content requirement for public works — the rule was published in the official gazette on Aug 31. Construction devours 60% of the country's steel, so that spending becomes a lever for domestic mills instead of imports. It's part of Plan México: Sheinbaum wants "que la mayor parte del acero que se usa en México se adquiera aquí."

🇲🇽🌎 <u>PETRO SELLS OUT UNAM IN TWO HOURS</u>

Colombia's Gustavo Petro filled UNAM's biggest auditorium in two hours flat for a lecture arguing that capitalist robotization breeds fascism — and Mexico's Fondo de Cultura Económica, run by Paco Ignacio Taibo II, will publish his book. It's his first trip since leaving office, and he chose Mexico; Sheinbaum welcomed him with a simple "bienvenido presidente Petro."

🇲🇽📈 Tomorrow Sheinbaum delivers her Second Report. The numbers she brings: economy strong, homicides down, peso holding. "The Mexican economy is doing very well, despite the tariffs." — Claudia Sheinbaum, ahead of her Segundo Informe July inflation 3.12%; Q2 GDP +1.5%; daily homicides down 51%; the National Guard at 130,000 after seven years. The Informe is Sept 1 — no mañanera tomorrow.

🇲🇽🎨 The plan doesn't "fix" teachers — it trusts them. "This isn't about training teachers — they already have enormous experience." — Claudia Sheinbaum, mañanera, Aug 31 The emotional-health strategy gives teachers methodology and psychological backup rather than a script, working collectively with families and students. Teachers lead; the state supports.
